answer: Because the timing is recorded against the river challenge, the comet audit can replay the inlet history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 114 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. A scripted farm thus has to pad 35 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
